query: Which single primary endpoint will we declare (e.g., time-to-occlusion) and what are the assumed effect sizes and variances used for its power calculation?

response.query: Which single primary endpoint will we declare (e.g., time-to-occlusion) and what are the assumed effect sizes and variances used for its power calculation?
response.answer: The primary endpoint is time-to-occlusion with an assumed effect size of 20% reduction and variance of 0.1 for power calculation.

results.title: Medicare Program; Changes to the Hospital Inpatient ...
results.content: Among the policy changes that we are making are: Changes to the classification of cases to the diagnosis-related groups (DRGs); changes to the long-term care (LTC)-DRGs and relative weights; changes in the wage data, labor-related share of the wage index, and the geographic area designations used to compute the wage index; changes in the qualifying threshold criteria for and the approval of new technologies and medical services for add-on payments; changes to the policies governing postacute care transfers; changes to payments to hospitals for the direct and indirect costs of graduate medical education; changes to the payment adjustment for disproportionate share rural hospitals; changes in requirements and payments to critical access hospitals (CAHs); change[...]oping the impact analysis presented below are taken from the March 2004 update of the FY 2003 MedPAR file and the March 2004 update of the Provider Specific File that is used for payment purposes.
